exercises.name: Low Inclined Dumbbell Chest Press
exercises.why: Targets the clavicular head (upper chest) at a 15-30 degree incline while reducing anterior shoulder impingement.
cues: Keep shoulder blades retracted and depressed
Lower dumbbells with elbows at roughly 45-60 degrees
Drive up and slightly inward without clacking dumbbells

exercises.name: Flat Barbell Bench Press
exercises.why: Primary compound movement for mid-sternal pectoralis major mass, engaging triceps and anterior deltoids.
cues: Plant feet firmly on the floor and arch upper back slightly
Touch lower chest with control before driving upward
Keep wrists stacked directly over forearms

exercises.name: Flat Dumbbell Press
exercises.why: Allows convergent pressing path and deeper stretch at the bottom than a fixed barbell.
cues: Lower dumbbells with elbows at 45 degrees
Feel stretch across pecs before pressing
Squeeze pecs at lockout

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
exercises.why: Biases upper pectoralis fibers and anterior delts with progressive barbell overload.
cues: Set bench angle to 30 degrees
Lower bar smoothly to upper collarbone line
Drive up and back towards eye line

exercises.name: Seated Back Supported Cable Fly
exercises.why: Maintains constant tension at peak contraction where free weights lose resistance.
cues: Keep chest up and shoulders pinned to back support
Think of hugging a wide tree with soft elbows
Squeeze pecs for 1 second at full closure

exercises.name: Standing Cable Crossover (High to Low)
exercises.why: Biases the sternocostal and abdominal heads (lower chest) following the natural fiber angle.
cues: Stagger stance with slight forward torso lean
Bring hands together down towards hip crease
Control eccentric return without letting shoulders roll forward

exercises.name: Standing Cable Crossover (Low to High)
exercises.why: Biases upper chest fibers in an upward diagonal sweep with steady cable resistance.
cues: Set pulleys at lowest peg
Sweep hands upward and inward to chest height
Focus on upper chest contraction at the apex

exercises.name: Pec Deck / Machine Fly
exercises.why: Fixed mechanical path provides pure horizontal adduction with zero stabilizer fatigue.
cues: Adjust seat so handles align with mid-chest
Keep elbows slightly bent and shoulders down
Pause briefly when pads touch

exercises.name: Chest Press Machine
exercises.why: Safe, high-threshold motor unit recruitment for pecs without balancing free weights.
cues: Set seat height so handles cross mid-nipple line
Keep shoulder blades pressed back against pad
Press smoothly without locking elbows hard

exercises.name: Knuckled Push Ups (Bodyweight)
exercises.why: Neutral wrist orientation relieves wrist strain while building chest, shoulder and core stability.
cues: Form fists on floor directly under shoulders
Maintain straight rigid plank posture
Lower chest smoothly to 1 inch off the floor

exercises.name: Standard Push Ups
exercises.why: Foundational closed-chain pressing exercise building chest endurance and serratus anterior function.
cues: Hands shoulder-width apart
Core tight, glutes engaged
Elbows track at 45 degrees back

exercises.name: Decline Dumbbell Press
exercises.why: Emphasizes lower sternal chest fibers with minimal shoulder joint stress.
cues: Secure shins under decline bench pads
Lower weights with control to lower chest
Press upward in a smooth convergent arc

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
exercises.why: Deep loaded stretch on the clavicular pec fibers at the bottom of the movement.
cues: Maintain 15-20 degree bend in elbows throughout
Open arms wide until comfortable stretch
Bring dumbbells together focusing on upper chest

exercises.name: Chest Dips (Bodyweight or Assisted)
exercises.why: Forward lean maximizes lower chest recruitment with high motor unit activation.
cues: Lean torso 30 degrees forward and tuck chin
Allow elbows to flare slightly outward
Lower until upper arms are parallel to floor

exercises.name: Incline Smith Machine Press
exercises.why: Guided track allows safe overload to absolute muscular failure on upper chest.
cues: Align bench so bar lowers to upper chest
Drive elbows straight up through the guided track
Control 3-second negative each rep

exercises.name: Single Arm Cable Chest Press
exercises.why: Unilateral pressing challenges pecs with rotational core anti-extension stability.
cues: Staggered athletic stance with cable at chest height
Press forward with punch-like control
Keep hips and shoulders square forward

exercises.name: Floor Press (Dumbbell or Barbell)
exercises.why: Floor stop eliminates hyper-extension of shoulder capsule while building tricep and mid-chest power.
cues: Lie flat on floor with knees bent
Lower elbows until triceps kiss floor softly
Pause for a beat before pressing up

exercises.name: Neutral Grip Dumbbell Press
exercises.why: Palms-facing grip creates a shoulder-friendly pressing angle for trainees with impingement.
cues: Keep palms facing each other throughout
Tuck elbows closer to ribs
Drive straight up without flaring

exercises.name: Front lat / Upper Back Pulldown
exercises.why: Builds back width and thickness by pulling through the coronal plane into lat insertion.
cues: Grip slightly wider than shoulders
Drive elbows down and back towards back pockets
Avoid excessive torso swinging

exercises.name: Bodyweight Pull Ups (Pronated)
exercises.why: Gold standard vertical pull engaging lats, teres major, lower traps, and core stability.
cues: Start from dead hang with active shoulders
Pull chest toward bar by driving elbows down
Lower under strict control without kipping

exercises.name: One Arm Dumbbell Rows (Lats s/s Upper Back focused)
exercises.why: Unilateral row corrects muscular imbalances and allows deep lat stretch and squeeze.
cues: Hinge torso parallel to bench or hip hinge
Pull dumbbell towards hip crease keeping arm close
Hold contraction at the top for 1 count

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row (Neutral Grip)
exercises.why: Develops mid-back thickness (rhomboids, middle traps) with stable foot bracing.
cues: Sit upright with slight natural spine arch
Lead with elbows and retract scapulae
Squeeze mid-back without leaning backward

exercises.name: Barbell Bent Over Row
exercises.why: Heavy compound builder for spinal erectors, lats, traps, and posterior chain.
cues: Hinge hips back at 45 degree torso angle
Pull bar smoothly into belly button
Maintain neutral spine without rounding lumbar

exercises.name: Chest Supported T-Bar Row
exercises.why: Isolates back musculature while fully eliminating lower back spinal fatigue.
cues: Pin chest to pad and keep chin neutral
Drive elbows back high for upper back or low for lats
Pause 1 second at full squeeze

exercises.name: Close Grip Lat Pulldown (V-Bar)
exercises.why: Neutral wrist orientation provides a deep stretch on outer lats with reduced elbow torque.
cues: Lean back slightly 10-15 degrees
Pull attachment to upper chest
Let arms extend fully at top for deep stretch

exercises.name: Single Arm Lat Pulldown (Kneeling or Seated)
exercises.why: Aligns the line of pull directly with individual lat fibers for maximum contraction.
cues: Reach high to feel full stretch on side of ribcage
Drive elbow directly down to hip bone
Keep torso steady without twisting excessively

exercises.name: Straight Arm Cable Pullover
exercises.why: Isolates lats without bicep involvement through pure shoulder extension.
cues: Soft bend in elbows locked in place
Hinge slightly at hips and sweep hands down to thighs
Feel lats contract hard at the bottom

exercises.name: Meadows Row (Landmine)
exercises.why: Pronated grip landmine row delivers exceptional upper lat and teres recruitment.
cues: Stand perpendicular to barbell collar in hip hinge
Pull with overhand grip leading with elbow high
Use wrist strap for secure grip if needed

exercises.name: Chin Ups (Supinated Grip)
exercises.why: Combines heavy lat engagement with strong biceps activation through a supinated pull.
cues: Palms facing you shoulder-width apart
Pull chest to bar leading with chest up
Lower under strict 3-second control

exercises.name: Face Pull (Rope attachment)
exercises.why: Strengthens rear delts, infraspinatus, and rhomboids to restore shoulder posture balance.
cues: Set pulley at eye height
Pull rope towards bridge of nose while externally rotating hands
End in a double-bicep pose position

exercises.name: Inverted Bodyweight Row
exercises.why: Horizontal pull balancing push-to-pull ratios with minimal lower back shear load.
cues: Set bar at waist height on rack or Smith machine
Hang underneath with body in rigid straight plank
Pull chest up to touch bar

exercises.name: Dumbbell Pullover
exercises.why: Loaded stretch on lats, serratus anterior, and ribcage expansiveness.
cues: Lie crosswise or lengthwise on flat bench
Cup inner plate of dumbbell with both palms
Lower weight behind head with soft elbows then return to eye line

exercises.name: Barbell Shrugs
exercises.why: Overloads upper trapezius muscle belly through pure scapular elevation.
cues: Hold bar with clean overhand grip shoulder-width
Elevate shoulders directly towards ears
Hold 1 second at apex, no rolling

exercises.name: Cable Shrugs
exercises.why: Smooth constant cable pull matches natural upward and inward trapezius line of drive.
cues: Stand centered between low cable attachments or bar
Shrug shoulders straight up and slightly in
Lower with 2-second control

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrugs
exercises.why: Neutral side-grip allows natural scapular elevation without barbell rubbing thighs.
cues: Hold heavy dumbbells at sides
Elevate shoulders as high as possible towards ears
Avoid rolling shoulders; keep movement vertical

exercises.name: Machine High Row
exercises.why: Diagonal pulling vector engages latissimus dorsi and lower trapezius simultaneously.
cues: Adjust seat so feet are flat on floor
Pull handles down and back towards ribs
Control release until full overhead stretch

exercises.name: Behind the back Cable lateral Raise
exercises.why: Places lateral deltoid under continuous tension throughout the entire abduction arc.
cues: Cable set at wrist/hip height behind back
Lead with elbow raising arm to shoulder level
Control lowering phase without swinging torso

exercises.name: Seated Side Lateral Dumbbell Raises
exercises.why: Eliminates leg drive and momentum to isolate the medial deltoid head.
cues: Sit upright with slight forward torso lean
Raise dumbbells out to sides leading with elbows
Pause at shoulder level before slow descent

exercises.name: Cross Cable 45 degree Rear Delt Fly
exercises.why: Isolates the posterior deltoid along its exact 45-degree fiber orientation.
cues: Cross cables without handles holding cable balls
Keep slight bend in elbows and sweep arms backward
Squeeze rear delts at the back without pinching traps

exercises.name: Seated Incline Front dumbbell Raise
exercises.why: Incline bench position keeps anterior deltoid under loaded tension from start to finish.
cues: Lie back on 45-60 degree incline bench
Raise dumbbells straight forward to eye level
Lower with control resisting gravity

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.why: Builds overhead pressing strength and anterior/lateral deltoid mass with freedom of joint angle.
cues: Seat back upright at 75-80 degrees
Elbows slightly tucked forward of shoulders
Press overhead in smooth arc without clacking weights

exercises.name: Standing Overhead Barbell Press (OHP)
exercises.why: Full-body overhead compound lift building shoulders, upper chest, triceps and core stability.
cues: Grip bar just outside shoulders with forearms vertical
Squeeze glutes and brace core tightly
Press straight up moving head back then through the window

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.why: Foundational medial deltoid builder for visual shoulder width.
cues: Slight forward lean with soft knees
Pour the water slightly with thumbs level or pinkies up
Stop at parallel with shoulders

exercises.name: Arnold Press
exercises.why: Rotational pressing recruits anterior and lateral delts across a broad functional arc.
cues: Start with palms facing chest at collarbone level
Rotate forearms outward as you press overhead
Finish at top with palms facing forward

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck (Rear Delt Fly)
exercises.why: Machine track prevents compensation and directly loads posterior deltoid heads.
cues: Chest firmly against pad with seat adjusted to shoulder height
Keep arms nearly straight with soft elbows
Drive elbows backward feeling rear shoulder contraction

exercises.name: Cable Front Raise (Rope or Bar)
exercises.why: Constant cable resistance challenges anterior deltoid through full flexion.
cues: Stand facing away or towards cable stack
Raise attachment smoothly to eye level
Lower under 3-second tension

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.why: Safe mechanical overload for delt mass without needing stabilizing spotters.
cues: Set handles at ear level when seated
Keep back flat against pad
Press up smoothly without snapping elbows at top

exercises.name: Lean-Away Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.why: Alters the angle of pull to maximize resistance at the top of the lateral raise range.
cues: Hold cable post with one arm and lean torso away at 20 degrees
Raise free arm outward to shoulder height
Control lowering phase smoothly

exercises.name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Fly (Prone or Bent Over)
exercises.why: Strengthens posterior chain and improves shoulder balance with free weights.
cues: Hinge torso forward parallel to floor or lie chest-down on incline bench
Raise dumbbells out to sides leading with pinkies
Squeeze rear shoulders at top

exercises.name: Upright Row (Cable or Dumbbell)
exercises.why: Engages lateral delts and upper traps; wide grip prevents internal rotation impingement.
cues: Take wide grip slightly outside shoulders
Pull attachment upward leading with elbows high
Stop when elbows reach shoulder height

exercises.name: Lu Raises (Full ROM Lateral Raise)
exercises.why: Full overhead range of motion develops scapular upward rotation and healthy shoulder mobility.
cues: Use light dumbbells and raise arms all the way overhead
Touch dumbbells softly at apex
Lower along wide perimeter with strict control

exercises.name: Egyptian Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.why: Leaning angle increases lateral delt tension specifically at mid-to-top range.
cues: Grasp pole leaning out at 30 degrees
Lift cable across body smoothly
Maintain strict tempo without jerking

exercises.name: Standing Neutral to Supination Rope Curls
exercises.why: Targets the brachialis in neutral grip and peaks biceps brachii as wrists supinate at top.
cues: Start with thumbs up on rope attachment
Supinate palms outward as you curl to chest height
Squeeze biceps and spread rope ends apart at top

exercises.name: Single Arm Preacher Curls (On 45-75 Degree Incline bench)
exercises.why: Arm placed in front of torso puts short head under peak overload at the fully stretched position.
cues: Armpit locked over top edge of bench
Lower weight smoothly without hyperextending elbow
Curl up without lifting upper arm off pad

exercises.name: Barbell Bicep Curl
exercises.why: Overload movement for total biceps brachii mass and forearm flexor strength.
cues: Grip bar shoulder-width with elbows pinned at sides
Curl bar upward in a smooth arc
Lower under controlled 3-second eccentric

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Bicep Curl
exercises.why: Cambered bar relieves wrist supination strain while heavily loading the biceps.
cues: Hold inner camber angles with wrists firm
Curl upward without swinging torso
Keep elbows stationary at rib cage

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.why: Shoulder hyperextension on incline bench maximizes long head bicep stretch for peak height.
cues: Set bench to 45-60 degrees with head supported
Let arms hang vertically behind torso
Curl dumbbells up while keeping elbows pinned back

exercises.name: Hammer Curls (Dumbbell)
exercises.why: Neutral grip shifts mechanical advantage onto the brachialis and brachioradialis for arm thickness.
cues: Keep palms facing each other throughout
Curl dumbbell up towards same-side shoulder
Control descent without swinging

exercises.name: Cable Bicep Curls (Straight Bar)
exercises.why: Provides uninterrupted muscle tension from full elbow extension to peak contraction.
cues: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart
Curl bar up to collarbones keeping elbows still
Feel constant tension on negative return

exercises.name: Concentration Curls
exercises.why: Tricep anchored to inner thigh eliminates all torso momentum for strict isolation.
cues: Sit on bench and brace back of upper arm against inner thigh
Curl weight towards opposite chest
Hold peak contraction for 1 count

exercises.name: Spider Curls (Chest on Incline Bench)
exercises.why: Forward arm angle places maximal mechanical tension at top of range for short head peak.
cues: Chest supported on 45-degree incline bench with arms hanging down
Curl bar upwards without shifting elbows forward
Squeeze hard at apex

exercises.name: Bayesian Cable Curl (Facing Away)
exercises.why: Loaded stretch behind the back throughout the rep creates deep muscle hypertrophy stimulus.
cues: Stand facing away from low pulley with arm extended behind
Curl handle forward keeping upper arm angled back
Control the stretch as arm extends back

exercises.name: Cross Body Hammer Curl
exercises.why: Curling across the torso isolates the brachialis and outer bicep head.
cues: Curl dumbbell across torso towards opposite pectoral
Keep wrist locked neutral
Lower slowly back to starting side

exercises.name: Reverse Barbell Curl
exercises.why: Pronated grip develops the brachioradialis and forearm extensor musculature.
cues: Grip bar with overhand (palms down) grip
Keep wrists straight and rigid throughout
Curl upward under strict control

exercises.name: High To Low Dual Rope Tricep Extension
exercises.why: Allows full shoulder clearance so triceps contract into complete extension without rope hitting hips.
cues: Use dual ropes on high pulley for full range of motion
Lock elbows at ribs and drive hands down and back
Squeeze triceps at lockout for 1 full second

exercises.name: Single arm overhead DUMBBELL Tricep Extension
exercises.why: Overhead arm angle places the long head of the triceps in loaded stretch.
cues: Sit upright supporting elbow with opposite hand if needed
Lower dumbbell behind head until deep tricep stretch
Extend arm upward to full lockout

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (Straight or V-Bar)
exercises.why: Overloads lateral and medial heads with stable joint path and high tension.
cues: Pin elbows to ribcage with slight torso lean
Push bar straight down to thighs
Control eccentric return to 90 degrees

exercises.name: Skull Crushers / Lying Triceps Extension (EZ-Bar)
exercises.why: Free weight long and medial tricep builder with high eccentric loading.
cues: Lie flat on bench holding EZ bar with narrow grip
Lower bar towards forehead or crown by bending elbows
Extend elbows back up without flaring outward

exercises.name: Close Grip Barbell Bench Press
exercises.why: Heavy compound exercise maximizing triceps mechanical tension with high loads.
cues: Hands placed shoulder-width apart (not too narrow)
Tuck elbows close to torso as bar lowers
Press upward focusing on tricep extension

exercises.name: Overhead Cable Tricep Extension (Rope)
exercises.why: Maintains constant stretch tension on the triceps long head unlike free dumbbells.
cues: Face away from pulley in staggered lunge stance
Bend elbows behind head feeling deep stretch
Extend arms forward and outward spreading ropes

exercises.name: Dips for Triceps (Parallel Bars)
exercises.why: Upright torso posture channels bodyweight resistance directly through triceps.
cues: Keep torso as upright as possible without forward lean
Lower until elbows reach 90 degrees
Push through palms to lockout

exercises.name: Bench Dips
exercises.why: Accessible tricep burner targeting lockout strength with bodyweight or plate.
cues: Hands on edge of bench behind hips
Lower hips close to bench by bending elbows straight back
Press up through palms

exercises.name: Cable Kickbacks
exercises.why: Cable line provides peak resistance at complete elbow extension.
cues: Hinge torso forward with elbow locked parallel to ribs
Extend forearm backward until arm is completely straight
Hold contraction for 1 second

exercises.name: JM Press (Smith or Barbell)
exercises.why: Hybrid between close-grip bench and skull crusher for heavy tricep mass.
cues: Lower bar directly toward chin or clavicle with elbows tucked
Keep wrists straight and press up forcefully
Control the eccentric tempo

exercises.name: Cross-Body Cable Tricep Extension
exercises.why: Aligns the line of pull with the natural anatomical angle of the tricep heads.
cues: Hold cable without handles across chest
Extend arm diagonally outward across the body
Lock out tricep with zero wrist flexion

exercises.name: Diamond Push Ups
exercises.why: Narrow hand placement shifts primary load onto lateral and medial tricep heads.
cues: Join index fingers and thumbs to form diamond under chest
Lower chest to hands keeping elbows tucked
Press up through palms to lockout

exercises.name: Heels Elevated Dumbbell Goblet Squat
exercises.why: Heel elevation increases knee flexion and shifts load onto the rectus femoris and vastus medialis.
cues: Elevate heels on wedges or weight plate
Hold dumbbell vertically at chest
Descend upright driving knees forward over toes

exercises.name: Leg Extension (Top Partials)
exercises.why: Overloads the rectus femoris at peak shortened contraction where vastus medialis fires hardest.
cues: Perform reps only in top 30-40% of knee extension
Squeeze quads rock-hard at top of every rep
Control the descent without dropping weight stack

exercises.name: Leg Extension (Bottom Partials)
exercises.why: Overloads quads in the loaded stretched position to trigger mechanical tension hypertrophy.
cues: Perform reps only in bottom 40-50% out of deep knee bend
Maintain smooth continuous tension without resting at bottom
Push out of stretch with control

exercises.name: Leg Extension (Full ROM)
exercises.why: Pure knee extension isolation targeting all four quadriceps heads without spinal compression.
cues: Align knee joint axis with machine pivot point
Extend shins upward smoothly to horizontal
Pause 1 second at top before slow 3-second descent

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.why: The ultimate lower body compound builder for quadriceps, glutes, adductors and systemic strength.
cues: Brace core with diaphragmatic 360-degree breath
Sit hips back and down between knees
Drive floor away while maintaining chest angle

exercises.name: Barbell Front Squat
exercises.why: Anterior barbell placement forces upright torso posture and pure quadriceps knee-dominant drive.
cues: Clean rack or cross-arm grip with elbows driven high
Keep chest tall throughout entire descent
Push knees forward tracking in line with toes

exercises.name: Hack Squat (Machine)
exercises.why: Guided back support removes balance limits, letting you safely push quads to true failure.
cues: Place feet low on platform shoulder-width
Squat down into deep knee flexion
Drive through midfoot without bouncing at bottom

exercises.name: Leg Press (Quad Focused - Low Foot Placement)
exercises.why: Low platform stance maximizes knee flexion and quad engagement while sparing lower back.
cues: Feet placed lower on sled hip-width apart
Lower carriage smoothly until knees reach 90 degrees or deeper
Press up without snapping knees into hyperextension

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Quad Focused)
exercises.why: Unilateral quad overload with upright torso driving intense quad load and correcting imbalances.
cues: Rear foot laces down on bench behind you
Keep torso upright as front knee drives forward
Drive through front midfoot to stand

exercises.name: Walking Lunges (Dumbbell or Barbell)
exercises.why: Dynamic unilateral movement challenging quads, glute stabilizers, and knee tracking.
cues: Take controlled strides keeping chest proud
Lower back knee gently toward floor
Push off front foot into next stride seamlessly

exercises.name: Sissy Squats (Bodyweight or Weighted)
exercises.why: Extreme loaded stretch on the rectus femoris across hip extension and knee flexion.
cues: Lean torso back as knees push far forward
Keep hips locked in extension
Press through toes to return upright

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
exercises.why: Fixed vertical track allows placing feet forward to emphasize pure quadriceps loading.
cues: Position feet slightly forward of bar
Lower smoothly with hips sinking between heels
Drive up smoothly against bar track

exercises.name: Step Ups (Dumbbell - Box or Bench)
exercises.why: Functional unilateral single-leg drive with high quad and glute recruitment.
cues: Step onto knee-height box with whole foot
Drive through lead heel without pushing off trailing toes
Control the step-down phase under slow tempo

exercises.name: Machine ADDUCTIONS
exercises.why: Develops adductor magnus and longus for inner thigh mass and knee stabilization.
cues: Set pads wide to comfortable stretch position
Squeeze knees together smoothly
Hold 1 second at full inner squeeze

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curls
exercises.why: Isolates the knee flexion function of the hamstrings with hip extension stretch.
cues: Keep hips pressed firmly down against pad
Curl heels up smoothly toward glutes
Resist the negative phase for 3 seconds

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.why: Flexed hip position puts hamstrings under stretch for superior hypertrophy outcomes.
cues: Lock thigh pad down snugly to prevent hips lifting
Curl heels back under seat as far as possible
Control the return until legs are almost straight

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlifts
exercises.why: Loaded eccentric stretch targeting hamstring origins and glute-ham tie-in.
cues: Hinge hips backward keeping shins nearly vertical
Keep dumbbells sliding close along legs
Stop at mid-shin when hamstrings are fully stretched

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
exercises.why: Heaviest hamstring hip-hinge builder overloading the posterior chain through loaded stretch.
cues: Soft unlock in knees and hinge hips back towards wall
Keep lats packed and bar close to shins
Drive hips forward to stand tall

exercises.name: Standing Single Leg Curl (Machine or Cable)
exercises.why: Unilateral knee flexion corrects side-to-side hamstring strength imbalances.
cues: Brace torso against machine pad
Curl heel up towards buttock under control
Lower slowly without letting weight stack touch

exercises.name: Glute Ham Raise (GHR)
exercises.why: Works hamstrings across both knee flexion and hip extension simultaneously.
cues: Secure ankles under rollers with knees on pad
Lower body forward under control keeping hips extended
Pull back up by contracting hamstrings

exercises.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
exercises.why: Proven gold-standard eccentric hamstring exercise for injury prevention and strength.
cues: Kneel with ankles anchored securely
Lower torso forward as slowly as possible resisting with hamstrings
Catch with hands and push back up

exercises.name: Good Mornings (Barbell)
exercises.why: Hip hinge movement overloading hamstrings and spinal erectors with long moment arm.
cues: Rest bar on upper traps with soft knees
Hinge hips straight back keeping flat back
Feel stretch in hamstrings and return with glute squeeze

exercises.name: Swiss Ball / Slider Hamstring Curl
exercises.why: Active hip bridge combined with knee curl creates intense cramping hamstring contraction.
cues: Lie on back and bridge hips up with heels on ball/sliders
Curl heels in towards glutes keeping hips elevated
Extend legs back under control

exercises.name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift (Dumbbell)
exercises.why: Unilateral hinge builds hamstring stability, balance, and foot/ankle proprioception.
cues: Stand on one foot with soft knee bend
Hinge forward reaching dumbbell towards floor as back leg extends
Keep hips square to floor without twisting

exercises.name: B-Stance Romanian Deadlift (Kickstand)
exercises.why: Toe-kickstand provides balance support while loading 90% of weight onto working hamstring.
cues: Step one toe 6 inches behind working foot as kickstand
Hinge hips back feeling pure stretch on front leg hamstring
Drive up through front heel

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
exercises.why: Horizontal cable vector provides constant hinge resistance without spinal compression.
cues: Straddle low pulley facing away holding rope between legs
Hinge hips back letting hands travel behind knees
Snap hips forward into glute contraction

exercises.name: Machine Hip Thrust
exercises.why: Locks in setup angle and eliminates barbell bruising to overload glutes in full extension.
cues: Belt or pad across pelvic hip crease
Drive through heels pushing hips up to full lockout
Squeeze glutes at top and tuck chin slightly

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.why: Unrivaled horizontal hip extension overload maximizing gluteus maximus recruitment.
cues: Upper back resting across bench with padded bar on hips
Feet flat hip-width apart with vertical shins at top
Drive hips to parallel with floor and hold 1 count

exercises.name: Cable Glute Kickback
exercises.why: Isolates the gluteus maximus through pure hip extension with uninterrupted cable tension.
cues: Attach ankle cuff to low pulley with torso hinged 45 degrees
Drive working heel back and slightly outward
Hold squeeze at peak extension without arching lumbar

exercises.name: Seated Hip Abduction Machine
exercises.why: Directly targets gluteus medius and minimus for hip stability and upper glute shelf.
cues: Sit upright or lean slightly forward on seat
Push pads outward as wide as comfortable
Hold 1 second before controlled return

exercises.name: Glute Bridge (Dumbbell or Barbell)
exercises.why: Floor-based hip extension with zero lower back strain for focused glute contraction.
cues: Lie flat on floor with knees bent and feet flat
Place weight across hips
Drive through heels to bridge hips until straight alignment

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Glute Focused - Forward Lean)
exercises.why: Forward torso hinge and longer stride maximize glute stretch and eccentric load.
cues: Forward torso lean over front knee
Hips hinge back into deep glute stretch
Drive up through working heel

exercises.name: Hyperextensions (45 Degree Glute Focused)
exercises.why: Flared feet and rounded upper back deactivate spinal erectors to isolate glutes.
cues: Set pad just below hip crease with toes turned out 45 degrees
Round upper spine softly and squeeze glutes to rise
Stop at neutral hip alignment, do not overextend

exercises.name: Frog Pumps
exercises.why: External hip rotation paired with bridging causes massive glute pump and metabolic stress.
cues: Lie on back with soles of feet pressed together (butterfly pose)
Drive outer edges of feet down and bridge hips up
Squeeze glutes at the top

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through (Glute Bias)
exercises.why: Safe hip hinge teaching posterior chain mechanics with strong peak glute lockout.
cues: Reach back through legs on hinge
Snap hips through with powerful glute squeeze
Stand tall without leaning back

exercises.name: Standing Cable Abduction
exercises.why: Loads gluteus medius standing to challenge pelvic level stability.
cues: Ankle cuff on low pulley
Abduct leg out to side with foot pointing forward
Hold top position for a beat

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise (Smith Machine)
exercises.why: Straight-leg extension fully engages the gastrocnemius with heavy progressive overload.
cues: Balls of feet on calf block with heels dropping deep
Press through big toes into full plantarflexion
Hold top for 1 full second and bottom stretch for 2 seconds

exercises.name: Seated Machine Calf Raises
exercises.why: Bent knee position places gastrocnemius in active insufficiency to isolate the soleus.
cues: Knee pad secured over lower thighs
Drop heels deep into full ankle dorsiflexion
Drive up onto toes pausing at the apex

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Single Leg Calf Raise
exercises.why: Unilateral calf loading improves ankle stability and balances left-to-right development.
cues: Hold dumbbell in working side hand and balance with free hand
Lower heel below step level for deep stretch
Press straight up onto ball of foot

exercises.name: Leg Press Calf Raise
exercises.why: High load capacity with zero spinal compression for high-volume calf stimulus.
cues: Balls of feet on lower lip of sled with heels free
Push sled away by flexing ankles forward
Keep knees softly unlocked (never hyper-extended)

exercises.name: Donkey Calf Raise
exercises.why: Hinged hip position stretches hamstrings and places gastrocnemius in optimal length-tension.
cues: Hinge 90 degrees at hips with back pad resting on sacrum
Deep drop at the bottom of each rep
Explode up onto toes and pause

exercises.name: Tibialis Raises
exercises.why: Strengthens tibialis anterior to balance calf pull and prevent shin splints and knee pain.
cues: Lean buttocks against wall with heels 1-2 feet out
Pull toes up towards shins as high as possible
Control descent without slapping floor

exercises.name: Core: Planks (Isometric Hold)
exercises.why: Develops anti-extension spinal stability, transversus abdominis bracing, and shoulder endurance.
cues: Forearms on floor with elbows under shoulders
Posterior pelvic tilt with glutes and quads squeezed hard
Do not allow lower back to sag

exercises.name: Core Stability: Side Planks
exercises.why: Strengthens the quadratus lumborum and obliques in lateral anti-flexion stability.
cues: Stack feet or stagger for balance with elbow under shoulder
Elevate hips until body forms straight diagonal line
Hold steady breathing smoothly

exercises.name: Abs: Declined Reverse Crunches
exercises.why: Posterior pelvic tilt pulls pelvis towards ribcage to emphasize lower rectus abdominis fibers.
cues: Grip top handles on decline bench
Curl knees up towards chest lifting pelvis off bench
Lower hips under strict control without swinging

exercises.name: Abs: Oblique Crunches
exercises.why: Targets internal and external obliques through controlled lateral trunk flexion.
cues: Lie with knees dropped softly to one side
Curl ribcage diagonally towards hip
Squeeze side ab wall at the peak

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raises
exercises.why: Advanced anterior core movement pulling pelvis into posterior tilt against gravity.
cues: Hang from pull-up bar with active shoulders
Raise legs by curling pelvis up towards chest (not just hip flexion)
Lower under 3-second control without swinging

exercises.name: Cable Woodchoppers (High to Low)
exercises.why: Rotational core power exercise engaging obliques and transverse abdominis dynamically.
cues: Hold handle with both hands outside high pulley
Rotate torso down across opposite knee pivoting back foot
Control the return with core bracing

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollouts
exercises.why: Intense anti-extension challenge building deep core wall tension at long muscle lengths.
cues: Kneel on mat with wheel under shoulders
Roll forward maintaining posterior pelvic tilt
Pull back using abs and lats without sagging lower back

exercises.name: Cable Kneeling Crunch
exercises.why: Allows progressive weighted overload on the rectus abdominis while keeping hips fixed.
cues: Hold rope behind neck kneeling on floor
Curl elbows down towards thighs flexing spine
Keep hips locked in position without sitting back

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.why: Teaches independent limb movement while maintaining flat lumbar spine anti-extension.
cues: Lie on back with arms up and knees at 90 degrees
Press lower back flat into floor
Extend opposite arm and leg smoothly, return and switch

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.why: Pure anti-rotation core exercise preventing torque on the lumbar spine.
cues: Hold cable handle at center of chest sideways to stack
Press arms straight out in front and hold 2 seconds
Resist the rotational pull of the cable

exercises.name: Captain Chair Knee Raise
exercises.why: Forearm support isolates rectus abdominis without grip fatigue or shoulder strain.
cues: Back against pad, forearms braced
Curl knees up towards chest rounding lower back slightly
Lower slowly without letting legs swing

exercises.name: Russian Twists
exercises.why: Strengthens oblique rotation and isometric hip flexor endurance.
cues: Balance on sit bones with feet elevated or heels down
Rotate shoulders and weight from side to side
Keep chest open and spine neutral

exercises.name: Incline Walk (Treadmill)
exercises.why: Low-impact Zone 2 aerobic stimulus that burns calories while preserving muscle and sparing joints.
cues: Set incline to 8-12% at 4.5-5.5 km/h
Do not hold onto handrails; swing arms naturally
Keep upright posture with engaged core

exercises.name: Stationary Cycling (Upright or Recumbent Bike)
exercises.why: Zero-impact cardiovascular conditioning that stimulates synovial fluid in knees and hips.
cues: Adjust seat height so knee has slight 10-degree bend at bottom of pedal stroke
Maintain smooth continuous cadence 75-85 RPM
Keep breathing steady through the nose if in Zone 2

exercises.name: Elliptical Trainer
exercises.why: Full-body cardiovascular work with zero ground impact shock on ankles, knees and spine.
cues: Push and pull actively through handles to recruit upper body
Keep whole foot in contact with footpads
Maintain steady heart rate target

exercises.name: Stair Climber (StairMaster)
exercises.why: High-calorie vertical climbing demanding both aerobic endurance and glute/quad drive.
cues: Step with whole foot on each step, not just toes
Rest fingertips lightly on rails for balance only
Keep torso upright without slumping forward

exercises.name: Outdoor Brisk Walk / Jog
exercises.why: Natural functional gait training providing natural vitamin D, mental reset, and cardiovascular endurance.
cues: Brisk pace where you can speak short sentences (Zone 2)
Land midfoot with soft knees
Keep head up and eyes forward

exercises.name: Cardio Warm Up: Cycling/ Elliptical trainer
exercises.why: Raises core body temperature, increases blood flow to working muscles, and lubricates joints.
cues: Maintain comfortable conversational pace
Gradually ramp up speed in final 2 minutes
Focus on rhythmic breathing

exercises.name: Cardio Warm Up: Recumbent Bike Or Incline TREADMILL walk
exercises.why: Gentle aerobic preparation to elevate heart rate safely without generating muscular fatigue.
cues: Maintain steady cadence
BPM around 110-130
Relax shoulders and breathe deep

exercises.name: Dynamic Stretchings
exercises.why: Full-body dynamic movements that take joints through full active range to prepare for lifting.
cues: Perform smooth continuous controlled repetitions
Do not bounce or force joints into pain
Coordinate movement with steady breathing

exercises.name: Dynamic Stretchings (Lower Body)
exercises.why: Mobilizes hips, knees, and ankles for squats and hinges with active muscle engagement.
cues: Perform controlled leg swings, walking knee hugs and hip openers
Gradually expand range with each rep
Keep core braced throughout

exercises.name: Cat & Camel
exercises.why: Gently mobilizes the entire spinal column through flexion and extension without axial loading.
cues: On hands and knees, slowly round spine up toward ceiling tucking chin
Smoothly reverse by sinking belly toward floor and looking up
Move smoothly with deep breathing

exercises.name: Dynamic Bird Dogs Followed By Isometric Holds
exercises.why: Activates posterior chain cross-body stability and glute medius while protecting lower back.
cues: On all fours, extend opposite arm and leg simultaneously
Hold straight line for 3-5 seconds without arching lower back
Keep hips perfectly square to floor

exercises.name: Arm Circles & Hugs (Dynamic)
exercises.why: Warms up glenohumeral joint capsule, rotator cuff, and chest/back tissue.
cues: Start with small circles, gradually making them larger
Alternate crossing arms across chest in dynamic hugs
Keep shoulders relaxed and down

exercises.name: Leg Swings (Front to Back)
exercises.why: Dynamically stretches hamstrings on forward swing and hip flexors on back swing.
cues: Hold wall for balance
Swing leg smoothly like a pendulum
Do not arch back excessively on rear swing

exercises.name: Leg Swings (Side to Side)
exercises.why: Dynamically stretches adductors on outward swing and abductors on inward cross.
cues: Stand facing wall with both hands on it
Swing leg across body and then out to side
Maintain tall upright torso

exercises.name: Worlds Greatest Stretch (Lunge with Thoracic Rotation)
exercises.why: Opens hip flexors, groin, hamstrings, and thoracic spine in one integrated movement.
cues: Step into deep lunge with both hands inside front foot
Reach inside elbow toward floor, then rotate chest toward ceiling
Follow hand with eyes at top of rotation

exercises.name: Thoracic Spine Open Books
exercises.why: Mobilizes the mid-back and chest without straining the lumbar spine.
cues: Lie on side with knees bent at 90 degrees
Sweep top arm all the way across body opening chest to floor
Keep knees glued together throughout

exercises.name: Inchworms with Push-Up
exercises.why: Stretches calves and hamstrings while activating shoulders, core and triceps.
cues: Hinge down touching floor with soft knees
Walk hands out into strong plank, perform push up
Walk feet up toward hands taking small steps

exercises.name: Deep Squat to Hamstring Stretch (Bootstrappers)
exercises.why: Prepares hips, knees, and ankles for deep squatting and hinges.
cues: Grab toes in deep squat with elbows pressing knees out
Keep hold of toes and push hips high into hamstring stretch
Sink back down tall into deep squat

exercises.name: Band Dislocates / Pass-Throughs
exercises.why: Increases shoulder internal and external rotation mobility safely with band elasticity.
cues: Hold light resistance band wide with straight arms
Sweep band up overhead and behind back without bending elbows
Bring back smoothly to front

exercises.name: Scapular Wall Slides
exercises.why: Activates serratus anterior and lower traps while mobilizing the rotator cuff.
cues: Back, head and forearms flat against wall in goalpost shape
Slide forearms upward without letting lower back arch off wall
Pull elbows down feeling mid-back squeeze

exercises.name: Walking Knee to Chest Hugs
exercises.why: Dynamically opens glutes and hip capsules while challenging single-leg balance.
cues: Pull knee tight into chest while standing tall on opposite toe
Hold 1 second and step smoothly into next rep
Keep chest high without rounding forward

exercises.name: Walking Heel to Butt (Quad Warm Up)
exercises.why: Dynamic stretch for quadriceps and hip flexors before running or lifting.
cues: Grasp ankle and pull heel gently to buttock with knees touching
Reach opposite arm tall toward ceiling
Step forward and alternate

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge Shifting (Cossack Dynamic)
exercises.why: Opens adductors, groin, and ankles in the frontal plane.
cues: Wide stance, sink hips to one side keeping other leg straight
Turn straight leg toes upward
Shift smoothly across to other side without standing fully

exercises.name: Wrist Circles & Mobility
exercises.why: Warms up wrist flexors and extensors before heavy pressing and gripping.
cues: Clasp hands and roll wrists in smooth fluid figures of eight
Gently extend and flex fingers
Place palms on floor on all fours to stretch lightly

exercises.name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Wall Rocks
exercises.why: Enhances ankle mobility for squat depth and prevents knee valgus collapse.
cues: Toes 3-4 inches from wall in half-kneeling or standing
Drive knee straight over second toe until knee touches wall
Keep heel pinned flat to floor

exercises.name: Hip 90/90 Transitions (Dynamic)
exercises.why: Mobilizes internal and external hip rotation simultaneously on the floor.
cues: Sit on floor with front and back legs bent at 90 degrees
Pivot knees smoothly across to opposite side without hands if possible
Keep spine tall throughout the switch

exercises.name: Downward Dog to Upward Dog Flow
exercises.why: Full anterior and posterior chain dynamic flow warming shoulders, spine and calves.
cues: Push hips high in down dog pressing heels to floor
Flow forward through plank into upward dog lifting chest
Breathe deeply through transitions

exercises.name: Chest Doorway Stretch (Static)
exercises.why: Relieves pec minor tightness and counters rounded shoulder posture.
cues: Place forearm on door frame with elbow at 90 degrees
Step forward with same-side leg until comfortable chest stretch
Hold and breathe smoothly without twisting spine

exercises.name: Kneeling Lat & Upper Back Stretch (Childs Pose with reach)
exercises.why: Lengthens latissimus dorsi and decompresses lower spine after heavy pulling or squats.
cues: Kneel sitting back on heels with arms outstretched forward on floor
Walk both hands diagonally to one side for targeted lat stretch
Breathe into side ribs and hold

exercises.name: Standing Quad Stretch (Static)
exercises.why: Restores resting length of the quadriceps and rectus femoris post leg workout.
cues: Hold wall for balance, grasp ankle and pull heel towards glutes
Keep knees aligned together and tuck pelvis slightly under
Avoid arching lower back

exercises.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch (Couch Stretch)
exercises.why: Releases tight psoas and iliacus muscles to reduce anterior pelvic tilt and lower back stress.
cues: Kneel in lunge with rear knee on mat and rear foot against wall/box
Squeeze rear glute and keep torso upright
Shift hips gently forward until deep stretch at front of hip

exercises.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch (Single or Double Leg)
exercises.why: Lengthens hamstring muscle bellies and relieves sciatic nerve tension.
cues: Sit on floor with legs extended straight in front
Hinge forward from hips leading with chest (not rounding back)
Hold ankles or feet and breathe deeply

exercises.name: Standing Calf Stretch (Wall push)
exercises.why: Lengthens gastrocnemius and Achilles tendon after running or calf training.
cues: Place hands on wall with back leg straight and heel pressed flat
Front knee bent, lean hips forward toward wall
Keep back heel glued down to feel deep calf stretch

exercises.name: Pigeon Pose / Glute Stretch
exercises.why: Deep external hip rotator and piriformis release to prevent sciatic irritation.
cues: Bring front knee bent across mat with back leg extended straight behind
Square hips toward mat and lower chest forward over front shin
Relax into the stretch with long exhales

exercises.name: Figure 4 Piriformis Stretch (Lying on Back)
exercises.why: Gentle on knees while effectively isolating deep glute and piriformis muscles.
cues: Lie on back, cross right ankle over left knee
Reach hands through to grasp behind left thigh and pull gently towards chest
Keep head and neck relaxed on floor

exercises.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch (Posterior Capsule)
exercises.why: Relieves posterior shoulder capsule stiffness after heavy pressing.
cues: Bring one arm across chest at shoulder level
Use opposite forearm to gently hug arm closer to chest
Keep shoulder down away from ear

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep & Lat Stretch
exercises.why: Lengthens triceps long head and lateral ribcage.
cues: Raise one elbow overhead and reach hand down between shoulder blades
Use other hand to guide elbow gently back and down
Maintain neutral spine without hyperextending ribs

exercises.name: Seated Butterfly Groin Stretch (Adductors)
exercises.why: Lengthens inner thigh adductor complex to restore hip abduction range.
cues: Sit tall with soles of feet together and knees falling outward
Hold feet with hands and gently press knees toward floor with elbows
Keep chest proud and breathe easy

exercises.name: Lying Spinal Twist
exercises.why: Rotational spinal decompression releasing lower back and lateral hip tension.
cues: Lie on back, hug right knee to chest, then drop it across body to the left
Look to the right with right arm extended on floor
Relax with slow abdominal breaths

exercises.name: Frog Stretch (Deep Adductors)
exercises.why: Intense hip opener targeting adductors and pelvic floor flexibility.
cues: On hands and knees, slide knees as wide apart as comfortable with inner feet flat
Sink forearms to floor and gently press hips backward
Hold where stretch is comfortable, breathe slowly

exercises.name: Biceps & Anterior Shoulder Wall Stretch
exercises.why: Releases bicep tendon and anterior deltoid after high volume pulling and curling.
cues: Place palm flat on wall behind you at shoulder height
Rotate chest and torso gently away from wall
Feel stretch run across bicep and front of shoulder

exercises.name: Neck & Upper Trapezius Lateral Stretch
exercises.why: Alleviates upper trapezius and levator scapulae tension from heavy shrugs or computer work.
cues: Drop right ear toward right shoulder gently
Rest right hand lightly on head without pulling hard
Reach left fingertips towards floor to deepen stretch

exercises.name: Forearm Flexor & Extensor Stretch
exercises.why: Prevents medial and lateral epicondylitis (golfers and tennis elbow) from heavy gripping.
cues: Extend arm forward with palm up, pull fingers back towards body with other hand
Reverse by turning palm down and pulling hand backward
Keep elbow straight

exercises.name: Seated Piriformis Chair Stretch
exercises.why: Accessible seated hip release for office workers and gym goers alike.
cues: Sit tall on edge of chair with one ankle crossed over opposite knee
Keep flat back and hinge forward from hips over the crossed shin
Hold until glute tension softens

exercises.name: Cobra / Sphinx Abdominal Stretch
exercises.why: Lengthens rectus abdominis and gently extends thoracic spine post core workout.
cues: Lie prone on stomach with hands under shoulders
Gently press chest up keeping pelvis pinned to floor
Keep shoulders relaxed down away from ears

exercises.name: Standing IT Band & Lateral Hip Stretch
exercises.why: Releases tension in tensor fasciae latae and lateral hip line.
cues: Cross right leg behind left leg with feet flat
Reach right arm overhead leaning torso toward left side
Push right hip out to side to feel long lateral stretch

exercises.name: Childs Pose (Deep Resting Pose)
exercises.why: Lowers nervous system arousal, restores parasympathetic state, and lengthens spine.
cues: Knees wide, big toes touching, sit hips all the way back onto heels
Rest forehead gently on floor with arms relaxed forward
Take slow 4-second inhales and 6-second exhales

techniques.superset: Perform 1 exercise followed immediately by another with minimal or no rest in between. Improves metabolic conditioning and workout density.
techniques.tri_set: Perform 3 exercises consecutively with no rest in between until the round is completed. Maximizes localized muscle fatigue.
techniques.giant_set: Perform 4 or more exercises back-to-back with zero rest between movements. High volume and cardiovascular stimulus.
techniques.drop_set: After finishing the set, immediately reduce the weight by ~10-20% without resting and continue reps to near failure.
techniques.double_drop: After reaching failure, reduce weight ~10-20% and rep out, then reduce weight again ~10-20% and rep to failure a second time.
techniques.rir: Reps In Reserve: how many more reps you could do before absolute muscular failure. Maintain 2-3 RIR on most sets, taking only the final set to near failure.
techniques.tempo: Speed of each repetition (eccentric / pause / concentric). Emphasize a controlled 3-4 second lowering phase to maximize muscle tension.
techniques.partials: After reaching full-range failure, perform partial reps through the strongest portion of the range of motion to extend the set safely.
techniques.rest_periods: Take 60 to 180 seconds between working sets to allow ATP-CP regeneration and nervous system recovery for maximum performance on the next set.
